Ancient homeolog pairing

Reordered by accepted pair membership

Chromosome-number distance matrix, reordered so each accepted pair sits adjacent to the diagonal instead of the pipeline's raw chromosome-number order -- resolves scattered/checkerboard-looking pairing into a clean pattern when it's just a numbering artifact; any structure that persists after reordering (e.g. tighter multi-pair blocks) is real signal beyond the individual pairs. See INTERPRETATION.md's "checkerboard" section. Undefined when there are no accepted pairs.

chr1940.038243chr220.083347-13.24803.27REAL ancient-homeolog pair, confirmed by Xie et al. 2026 Nature (doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10439-1): chr19+chr22 is an ancestral unbalanced chromosome fusion shared across all snow carps (~30Ma, their "wave 1", highest divergence/most-resolved fusion pair). HAP3/HAP4 carry the fused (f) chromosome (~69.5Mb, chr19+chr22 physically joined); HAP1/HAP2 retain the unfused (uf) ancestral pair. The windowed-heatmap match being confined to a block, not genome-wide, is the CORRECT signature for a physically fused ohnologue, not an artifact -- my earlier note here calling this an artifact was wrong and has been corrected. distance_ratio=3.27 reflects real but partial (not complete) sequence-level rediploidization at this locus, consistent with the paper's Ks-based dating. See OUTPUTS.md.
